recipes.name: Approval Workflow
recipes.description: Sequential approval chain: manager then admin (configurable). Sends approval notifications, handles approve/deny/return-for-info responses, enforces timeout reminders at halfway marks and escalates on full timeout. High-privilege requests always route through human review regardless of auto-rules. Emergency urgency uses shortened timeouts.

recipes.name: Audit & Reporting
recipes.description: Compile audit digests and compliance reports. Daily summary: requests received, approved, denied, escalated, expired, average time-to-approval. Weekly summary identifies bottleneck approvers. On-demand compliance report shows grants within a date range with full approval chains and justifications. Default daily end-of-day + weekly Monday — final cadence at trigger step.

recipes.name: Request Intake & Triage
recipes.description: Poll the configured inbox for new access request emails, parse structured fields, validate completeness, deduplicate against recent requests, classify privilege level, and create the immutable audit record. Emits the received event to kick off the approval workflow. Default polling cadence every 10 minutes — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_intake_triage","slug":"access-request-intake-and-triage","title":"Access request intake and triage","status":"draft","path":"operations_logistics/intake","domain":"operations_logistics","description":{"need":"Access requests arrive as ordinary messages among everything else, so the same ask classified request to the approval decision","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"complete-audit-trail","statement":"Every incoming access request is captured once, correctly classified, and never recipes.name: Contract Intake and Analysis
recipes.description: Pulls an incoming contract (email tags/folders or webhook), extracts text, identifies the contract type, and runs the six-pass structured analysis: key terms, financials, obligations, risk assessment, red flags, market comparison. Produces the structured record that downstream capabilities publish and alert on.

recipes.name: Deadline Reminder Sweep
recipes.description: Daily scan of all tracked contract deadlines — renewal dates, termination notice windows, obligation due dates, warranty expirations. Sends tiered reminders at 30 / 14 / 7 days via email (to submitter + configured recipients) and messaging (to the legal channel). Duplicate-suppressed via per-deadline reminder flags. Default daily morning; final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_deadline_reminders","slug":"contract-obligation-and-deadline-watch","title":"Contract obligation and deadline watch","status":"draft","path":"legal_compliance/deadlines","domain":"legal_compliance","description":{"need":"A contract's consequences are carried by dates that live inside it: notice windows, obligation due dates, warranty expiries. Nobody re-reads a signed contract to find them, so they arrive as surprises.","input":"Every tracked contract with the dates it carries, and the record of which of those dates have already been raised.","coreAction":"Decide which dates are close enough to matter, how urgent each has become, and who can actually act, without raising the same date at the same urgency twice.","output":"No date with a consequence passes without the person who could have acted on it having been told while there was still time."},"activities":[{"id":"survey","label":"Survey every tracked contract obligation and the date attached to it","kind":"observe"},{"id":"approach","label":"Judge which dates are close enough to matter and how urgent each has become","kind":"decide"},{"id":"suppress","label":"Set aside dates already raised at the same urgency","kind":"decide"},{"id":"raise","label":"Raise the date with the people who can act on it","kind":"act"},{"id":"escalate","label":"Escalate a date that keeps being raised and keeps being ignored","kind":"act"},{"id":"mark","label":"Record what was raised so the next pass does not repeat it","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"no-missed-contract-deadline","statement":"Nobody is surprised by a contract renewal, termination window, obligation or warranty deadline arriving unannounced.","successCriteria":["Every tracked date is raised at each level of urgency before it lapses","A date already raised at a given urgency is never raised again at that same urgency","A date that passed without anybody acting is treated as a miss regardless of whether the message was delivered"]}],"guidance":"Own visibility into every date a signed contract commits someone to: renewals, notice windows, obligations, warranties. recipes.name: knowledge base Publish and Risk Alert
recipes.description: Converts the structured review record into a knowledge base pages with full sections, sends the email summary to the submitter, and fires a messaging alert when red flag count meets the high-risk threshold. Updates the contract log and deadline tracker.

recipes.name: Audio Production
recipes.description: On approved script, synthesize each segment via TTS, stitch with 300ms silences via ffmpeg, verify duration, and deliver the MP3 for final review. On approval, save hook/voice/pacing preferences to memory.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_audio_production","slug":"audio-briefing-production","title":"Audio briefing production","status":"draft","path":"creative_design/audio","domain":"creative_design","description":{"need":"An approved script is not a listenable briefing, and hand editing every segment into one track is the step that stops briefings from shipping regularly.","input":"An approved multi segment script with host turns, a target runtime, and any pacing or intro material the adopter supplies.","coreAction":"Synthesize each segment as speech, join the segments into one coherent track with deliberate pacing between them, and judge the result against the runtime the script promised before calling it finished.","output":"A single finished audio file whose pacing and length were verified, ready for a listen and a final decision rather than for further editing."},"activities":[{"id":"read-script","label":"Read the approved script and its segment structure","kind":"observe"},{"id":"voice-choice","label":"Settle voice pairing and pacing against what has been approved before","kind":"decide"},{"id":"synthesize","label":"Synthesize each segment as speech","kind":"act"},{"id":"stitch","label":"Join segments into one track with the intended spacing","kind":"act"},{"id":"verify","label":"Check the finished track against the promised runtime","kind":"decide"},{"id":"deliver","label":"Hand over the finished file for a listen","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"clean-final-mp3","statement":"An approved script becomes a listenable, correctly paced final audio file without manual editing.","successCriteria":["Segment audio joins with natural pacing, verified by a duration check rather than by a successful render","The delivered file is ready for review, not a rough cut"]}],"guidance":"Turn an approved script into a finished audio file: synthesize each segment, join it into one coherent track, and verify the result actually sounds and runs right before calling it done. recipes.name: Script Drafting
recipes.description: Distill any source (pasted text, file, URL, upstream agent output) into a structured two-host script: headline finding, key facts, tensions, implications, open questions, then turn-by-turn segments with strict pacing. Human approves before any audio synthesis. Manual trigger — user supplies the source on demand.

recipes.name: In-Flight Experiment Significance Watch
recipes.description: Check every in-flight experiment against sample-size + duration guardrails and the significance threshold. Classify as RUNNING, WINNER, LOSER, or INCONCLUSIVE and prepare promote/revert/archive proposals for human review. Default weekly — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_experiment_watch","slug":"conversion-experiment-significance-watch","title":"Conversion experiment significance recipes.name: New Variant Proposals

recipes.name: Billing API Recovery Alerts
recipes.description: Listens for `budget.access.failure` from the weekly check and delivers a targeted Messages alert explaining why the agent is blind this week — expired credentials, rate limit, partial data, or empty billing — with provider-specific troubleshooting steps.

recipes.name: Weekly Cost & Resource Report
recipes.description: Pull last-7-day billing, compute WoW deltas against the rolling baseline, evaluate against the spending threshold, and alert via Messages ONLY if anomaly conditions are met — threshold breach, >50% service spike, new service appearance, or 4+-day acceleration. Silent when normal. Default weekly Monday 9:00 AM — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Daily Threshold Tracker
recipes.description: Every day, pull month-to-date spend plus today's run-rate, project the end-of-period total, and compare against the threshold. Stay SILENT when under budget; send a single concise alert via Messages ONLY when MTD or the projection crosses the threshold (or a sharp daily spike). Emit budget.threshold.exceeded on breach.

open.","coreAction":"Project the likely end-of-period total from the run rate and judge the trajectory rather than today's number, then stay quiet unless the projection or the actual crosses the recipes.name: Publish or Schedule Approved Draft
recipes.description: Listens to `review_decision.approved` events from this persona, reads the approved draft from the event's context_data, and dispatches it to the platform-specific destination connector — native LinkedIn post, X thread, Notion blog page, or Buffer scheduled queue. Always confirms via Messages with the published-artifact link or scheduled-time. Updates per-platform approvals memory.

recipes.name: Mid-Week Anomaly Check
recipes.description: Silent-unless-something-moved checkpoint. Compares partial-week metrics against expected trajectory derived from baselines. Alerts on deviations, silent when normal. Default Wednesday + Friday noon — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Weekly Performance Report
recipes.description: Compile the weekly report: WoW deltas, composite-scored rankings, anomaly detection against 4-week EWMA baselines, trend narrative, editorial recommendations. Default Monday 09:00 — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: legal platform Event Processing
recipes.description: Real-time webhook handler for legal platform envelope events. Fetches full envelope context, upserts into spreadsheet (envelope_id as idempotency key), posts messaging notifications to event-appropriate channels, and tracks signer velocity in memory.

recipes.name: Unsigned Contract Reminders
recipes.description: Daily sweep that finds unsigned contracts past the remind threshold and applies the escalation ladder: polite signer reminder (capped at 3) → direct messages + email to contract owner → manual_review escalation at 14+ days. Default daily weekday morning; final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Renewal Monitoring
recipes.description: Weekly scan for contracts with renewal dates inside the configured lookahead window. Fires tiered notifications: 60d informational → 30d reminder → 14d urgent. Per-contract notification state prevents duplicates. Default weekly Monday; final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_renewal_monitor","slug":"contract-renewal-window-watch","title":"Contract renewal window watch","status":"draft","path":"legal_compliance/deadlines","domain":"legal_compliance","description":{"need":"Renewal clocks run whether anyone is watching or not. recipes.name: Ask a Question
recipes.description: Receive a natural-language question via messaging, resolve follow-up context, generate safe SELECT SQL, execute against the database, deliver formatted result with the SQL and metadata. Event-listen on incoming messages.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_ask_question","slug":"live-database-question-answering","title":"Live database question answering","status":"draft","path":"data_ai/data-access","domain":"data_ai","description":{"need":"People who need a number wait for whoever can write the query, and the person who can write it spends their week writing them. recipes.name: Schema Refresh
recipes.description: Daily schema introspection with change detection. Updates the cache and notifies when new tables, altered columns, or dropped entities appear. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default daily 2am.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_schema_refresh","slug":"database-schema-picture-refresh","title":"Database schema picture refresh","status":"draft","path":"data_ai/data-access","domain":"data_ai","description":{"need":"Anything answering questions about a database works from a cached picture of its structure. recipes.name: Weekly Query Digest
recipes.description: Weekly rollup of question activity — most-asked patterns, most-queried tables, execution stats, rejection rate, suggestions for saved queries. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default Monday 9am.

recipes.name: Decision Support
recipes.description: On-demand structured decision analysis. User invokes with a decision context (e.g., 'hire full-time editor vs Fiverr freelancers'). Agent asks clarifying questions, researches each option, builds a weighted matrix, identifies risks and mitigations, defines 14-day success metrics + kill criteria.

recipes.name: Personal Briefing
recipes.description: Consolidated briefing that fuses niche intelligence research (grounded in user-defined sources and goals) + goal progress check-in + pending work accountability + prioritized action plan. One focused, readable message. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default daily 7am.

recipes.name: Weekly Review
recipes.description: Weekly retrospective. Reviews each active goal's weekly trend and surfaces next-week focus. Triages the week's captured ideas (accept to backlog / reject / defer). Surfaces decisions reaching their 14-day checkpoint. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default Sunday 6pm.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_weekly_review","slug":"goal-accountability-and-idea-triage-review","title":"Goal accountability and idea triage pile up unreviewed, and decisions that were supposed to be revisited never are.","input":"Each active goal with its observed activity and deadline, the ideas captured since the last review, and the recipes.name: Anomaly Response
recipes.description: On critical breach, capture evidence, correlate metrics, hypothesize root cause, escalate with a full incident report and remediation options. Event-chained off the monitoring loop.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_anomaly_response","slug":"database-anomaly-incident-diagnosis","title":"Database anomaly incident deserves","kind":"decide"},{"id":"options","label":"Set out the remediation options and what each would cost","kind":"decide"},{"id":"escalate","label":"Escalate to a person, changing nothing on the database","kind":"deliver"},{"id":"learn","label":"Record the operator's verdict so the next case of this shape is judged with recipes.name: Continuous Monitoring
recipes.description: Scheduled metric collection, baseline building during the silent learning period, then active monitoring with direction-aware thresholds. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default every 5 minutes.

(response time, throughput, connections, locks, cache, disk I/O)"],"default":"Response time + throughput","description":"Which dimensions to track and recipes.name: Backlog Scan
recipes.description: Scan the registered codebase for improvement candidates: TODOs / FIXMEs / HACK comments, portfolio-health hotspots, risk-matrix flags, deprecated dependency usage, architectural gaps from cross-project analysis. Compose each finding as a structured candidate and emit for triage. Does NOT implement — implementation waits for a human accept in uc_triage. Scan cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default hourly.

recipes.name: Implementation & PR Lifecycle
recipes.description: Event-listen on accepted triage decisions. For each accepted item: understand affected code, plan the diff, create a branch, apply changes, run tests (3 iteration max), commit, create PR via GitHub. Reacts to PR review comments via webhook — auto-fixes code-change requests, answers questions inline, escalates architectural concerns to the human.

recipes.name: Release Management
recipes.description: Gathers merged PRs since the last release, drafts release notes grouped by category, runs the full test suite, and presents the release candidate to the human for approval. On approval: tag via Git, emit release-accepted event. On rejection: memorize the reason, create follow-up backlog items.

recipes.name: Triage Pipeline
recipes.description: Event-listen on dev-clone.backlog.candidate. Presents each candidate to the human with accept / reject / defer actions. Rejection reasons persist in memory so similar candidates stop surfacing. Accept fans out to uc_implementation via event.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_triage","slug":"work-candidate-triage-gate","title":"Work candidate triage gate","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/work-intake","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"Anything that generates candidates will eventually generate more than anyone can recipes.name: Database Health Check
recipes.description: Runs read-only health queries against the configured database (connection pool, slow queries, table growth, replication lag, bloat, failed migrations). Compares against baselines. If the database is unreachable, surfaces that as its own Critical incident. Default daily 8 AM — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_db_health","slug":"database-health-check","title":"Database health check","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/observability","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"A connection pool filling up, a slow query count climbing, or replication falling behind is a performance indicator for days before it is an outage, and nobody looks until it is the outage.","input":"Read only health queries against one database, plus the rolling record of what those same queries returned on earlier passes.","coreAction":"Compare each health signal against its own recent history rather than a fixed number, and decide which movements are worth reporting and which are the database working normally.","output":"A health account naming what moved, against what history, and an explicit Critical when the database could not be reached at all."},"activities":[{"id":"query","label":"Run the read only health queries the engine supports","kind":"observe"},{"id":"compare","label":"Compare each signal against its own rolling history","kind":"decide"},{"id":"rank","label":"Decide which movements are worth someone's attention","kind":"decide"},{"id":"report","label":"Report the account, with unreachability raised as its own Critical","kind":"deliver"},{"id":"record","label":"Extend the rolling history so the next pass has something to compare against","kind":"act"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"db-problems-known-before-outage","statement":"A degrading connection pool, growing slow query count, or replication lag is known while it is still a performance indicator, not after it becomes an outage.","successCriteria":["Every check compares current metrics against the rolling baseline, not a static number.","Database unreachability is always surfaced as its own Critical incident, never folded silently into a generic failure."]}],"guidance":"Own catching database degradation early enough that it never becomes a surprise outage. recipes.name: Deploy Regression Correlation
recipes.description: Lists deployments in the scan window and cross-references timestamps with error spikes detected by the error scan. A deploy within 2 hours of a >20% error-rate jump is flagged as a regression with commit SHA, author, and rollback hint. Default daily 8 AM — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_deploy_correlation","slug":"deploy-regression-correlation","title":"Deploy regression correlation","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/observability","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"When errors jump, whoever is on call starts from zero on the question that matters most, which is what changed just before, and the answer is sitting in the deploy list nobody cross referenced.","input":"The deployment list for the window, the error rate series over the same window, and the size of correlation window the adopter considers meaningful.","coreAction":"Decide which error jumps are close enough to a deploy to be named as its regression, and which are merely near it in time and must be labelled as no more than possibly related.","output":"Named regressions carrying the commit, the author and a rollback hint, and a clean statement when no deploy in the window explains anything."},"activities":[{"id":"list","label":"List the deployments that landed inside the window","kind":"observe"},{"id":"align","label":"Line the deploy times up against the error rate series","kind":"observe"},{"id":"judge","label":"Decide which pairings are close enough to be called regressions","kind":"decide"},{"id":"deliver","label":"Name each regression with its commit, author and rollback hint, and soften the weak ones","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"bad-deploys-linked-to-cause","statement":"When errors spike shortly after a deploy, whoever is on call already has the commit and author in hand instead of starting from zero.","successCriteria":["A deploy within the configured correlation window of an error rate jump is named with commit SHA, author, and a rollback hint.","A weak or distant correlation is labeled 'possibly related' rather than asserted as a regression."]}],"guidance":"Own connecting error spikes back to the deploy that likely caused them, without crying wolf on coincidence. A raw infrastructure cloud such as builtin-aws-cloud also resolves to this type but has no deployment concept of its own, so the deploy list would have to come from somewhere else."},{"title":"An error monitor as the monitoring connector","connector":"sentry","connectorType":"monitoring","notes":"builtin-sentry carries release markers alongside error series, which is the pairing this correlation is easiest against. recipes.name: Application Error Scan
recipes.description: Pulls unresolved errors from the monitoring provider for the last N hours, classifies severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low) using data + memory, flags new error types and regressions, and contributes the application-errors section to the combined briefing. Default daily 8 AM — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Draft and Review
recipes.description: For each inbound message that needs a reply, loads the recipient's style profile + conversation context, composes a draft that matches the profile exactly, and routes through human review — or auto-sends if the contact has graduated. Updates the style profile from every human edit.

recipes.name: Codebase Feasibility Analysis
recipes.description: For each accepted idea, run a feasibility pass against the registered codebase: related code search, effort estimate from affected surface, benefit call. Produce the structured backlog record and emit it so downstream backlog systems (or a human curator) can finalize it.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_codebase_analysis","slug":"codebase-feasibility-analysis","title":"Codebase feasibility analysis","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/codebase-health","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"Effort and benefit estimates made without opening the code are guesses that read like facts, and a backlog built from them is a backlog nobody can plan against.","input":"An accepted idea, the registered codebase it would land in, and how deep a search the adopter is willing to pay for.","coreAction":"Let the code actually found, or its absence, drive the effort and benefit call, marking feasibility unknown rather than low when the search returns nothing.","output":"A backlog record a curator can trust, naming the related code found and the depth at which it was searched."},"activities":[{"id":"search","label":"Search the codebase for the code related to the idea","kind":"observe"},{"id":"surface","label":"Work out how much surface the change would touch","kind":"observe"},{"id":"estimate","label":"Let the evidence found, or its absence, drive effort and benefit","kind":"decide"},{"id":"record","label":"Produce the backlog record with what grounded it","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"backlog-items-grounded-in-real-code","statement":"An idea's effort and benefit estimate reflects what the codebase actually looks like, not a guess made without reading it.","successCriteria":["Every accepted idea produces a feasibility record backed by an actual code search, with feasibility marked unknown rather than low when the search returns nothing.","A codebase offline condition queues the idea for retry rather than producing an ungrounded estimate."]}],"guidance":"Own turning an accepted idea into a backlog item a human curator can trust, grounded in what the registered codebase actually contains. It survives verbatim in input_schema and is exactly what the connector_type resolves into on the charter."}],"lessons":[],"provenance":{"fromRecipes":["e51901e2-5b39-567a-b89b-890395eb1ed3"],"fromTemplates":["idea-harvester"],"sourceTemplateId":"idea-harvester"},"inputSchema":[{"name":"analysis_depth","type":"enum","options":["quick","standard","deep"],"default":"standard","description":"Quick = keyword-only search; Standard = keyword + file browse; Deep = + read matched files + context maps."}],"transformNotes":["input_schema.target_codebase (type connector_ref) was a second binding seam and is dropped. recipes.name: Idea Harvesting
recipes.description: Weekly scan across configured sources (messaging channels, knowledge base pages, Google Alerts, pasted URL queue). Extract 3-10 concrete candidates per source. Skip vague/meta content. Emit one event per candidate; candidates land in the triage queue.

recipes.name: Triage Pipeline
recipes.description: For each harvested idea, present to the human with accept/reject affordance. Every decision becomes memory training data so future harvests weight categories accordingly. Accepted ideas trigger the codebase-analysis capability; rejected ones stay in the harvest log with reason.

recipes.name: Incident Intake & Classification
recipes.description: Captures a new incident report with full detail, runs fuzzy-match duplicate detection against open incidents from the last 2 hours, classifies severity by impact (S1/S2/S3/S4), generates the structured record with escalation deadline and update cadence, persists it, and routes the severity-appropriate notification. Triggered on demand when a team member reports an incident.

recipes.name: Post-Incident Review
recipes.description: For resolved S1 and S2 incidents, waits a configurable settling period (default 24 hours) then generates a structured post-mortem: summary, timeline, impact, root cause, response metrics, action items, lessons learned. Queries memory for recurring root-cause categories in the last 90 days and flags systemic patterns. Presented via human approval before finalizing.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_postmortem","slug":"post-incident-review","title":"Post-incident review and prevention The v2 recipe fired on resolution and then waited a fixed delay, which is a self paced judgement wearing an event's clothes."},"personalizationNeeds":["Which severities deserve a written account at all, because writing one for everything guarantees none of them are read","Where prevention proposals should go so they become real work, because a proposal that lands nowhere is the reason the same incident recurs","How long this team needs before an account will be accurate, since the right settling period is a property of how they work"],"dependencies":[],"examples":[],"lessons":[],"provenance":{"fromRecipes":["6a86eaad-5306-5e13-81a1-930cf03972e6"],"fromTemplates":["incident-logger"],"sourceTemplateId":"incident-logger"},"inputSchema":[{"name":"postmortem_delay_hours","type":"number","default":24,"min":1,"max":72,"description":"How long to wait after resolution before generating the review. recipes.name: Lifecycle Tracking & Escalation
recipes.description: Maintains the live status board for every open incident: processes status updates into the timeline, resets escalation timers, enforces severity-based update cadences, auto-closes stale S4 items, and requests human closure confirmation when status transitions to resolved. Default escalation sweep every 15 minutes — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_tracking","slug":"open-incident-vigilance","title":"Open incident vigilance and escalation","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/incident-response","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"Incidents are rarely abandoned deliberately; Escalate on silence rather than on elapsed time alone, and watch that repeated nudges do not become noise a responder learns to ignore.","connectorTypes":[],"recommendedTrigger":{"kind":"self_paced","rationale":"Decide when to look from the state of the board itself: a serious incident with no update needs attention far sooner than a minor one, and an empty board needs none at all. Lower = faster response, higher alert fatigue."}]}

recipes.name: Monthly Deep Audit
recipes.description: Everything the weekly audit does, plus a cross-article contradiction pass over compiled wiki articles (title family clustering + body disagreement detection). More expensive than the weekly pass; opt-in. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default first-of-month 8am.

alone","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"contradictions-caught","statement":"Cross article contradictions are caught, not just per article staleness and orphan Lower = stricter."}],"transformNotes":["knob:stale_threshold_days: carries cadence \"weekly\". v3 moved the schedule to the charter's trigger; a cadence surviving in a knob is a binding where nobody looks for it. recipes.name: Weekly Health Audit
recipes.description: Run all three audit modes (persona memories, vector KBs, optional Obsidian vault), cap findings per category, queue every issue via manual_review with severity + recommended action, deliver a single checklist summary, and persist trend totals. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default Sunday 8am.

recipes.name: Sales Alert

recipes.name: Personalized Welcome Email

recipes.name: Lean Sweep
recipes.description: Runs the configured static-analysis CLI in the registered codebase, parses the JSON report, creates backlog ideas for each finding, deduplicates against prior sweeps, and posts a one-line summary. Default cadence is daily 8am — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step (post-commit and manual triggers also supported).

recipes.name: Baseline Refresh
recipes.description: Scheduled capability. Recalculates anomaly baselines (order-value mean / stdev, signup rate, field distributions) from the last 30 days of Supabase data. Keeps detection thresholds current as business patterns evolve. Default every 6 hours — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_baseline_refresh","slug":"database-anomaly-baseline-refresh","title":"Database anomaly baseline refresh","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/observability","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"Anomaly detection is only as honest as the baseline behind it, and a force, and knowledge of which past periods were abnormal by design.","coreAction":"Recompute the distributions detection depends on from what the business has actually been doing recently, and decide recipes.name: Event Routing & Anomaly Detection
recipes.description: Webhook-driven capability. Parses each Supabase row event, classifies by table + operation, enriches via REST fetches, posts formatted messaging layout cards to topic-specific messaging channels, sends welcome / confirmation emails via email with dedup, and runs inline anomaly detection with severity-tiered alerts. Event-driven; not configurable at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Weekly Digest
recipes.description: Scheduled capability. Compiles the week's activity across all monitored tables with week-over-week deltas and posts a formatted messaging layout digest to the operations summary channel. Default Monday 09:00 local — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: social platform Trend Digest
recipes.description: Fetch top posts from configured subreddits, dedup against a 30-day seen-posts index, cluster into themes with sentiment labels, assemble messaging-flavored markdown, and post to the configured channel. Default daily 09:00 UTC — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_digest","slug":"community-trend-digest","title":"Community discussion trend digest","status":"draft","path":"sales_marketing/community-channels","domain":"sales_marketing","description":{"need":"The communities where a product's users talk about it move faster than anyone can read, and a digest that pads itself to look consistent teaches its readers to skip it.","input":"The communities the adopter follows, the index of posts already covered, and the corrections reviewers have made to past digests.","coreAction":"Cluster genuinely new discussion into the few themes that actually ran, label the sentiment honestly, and ship fewer themes on a quiet day rather than stretching thin material.","output":"A short themed digest of what those communities actually discussed, delivered where the team reads, saying plainly when there was nothing."},"activities":[{"id":"fetch","label":"Pull recent activity from the followed communities","kind":"observe"},{"id":"dedupe","label":"Drop what previous digests already covered","kind":"act"},{"id":"cluster","label":"Cluster the remainder into the themes that genuinely ran","kind":"decide"},{"id":"label","label":"Label sentiment and decide what is worth a reader's attention","kind":"decide"},{"id":"deliver","label":"Deliver the digest, or say plainly that there was nothing","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"real-themes-not-padding","statement":"The digest reflects what the followed communities actually discussed in the period, never padded to look busier than it was.","successCriteria":["The digest ships fewer clusters on a quiet day rather than stretching thin content to hit the configured maximum","A period with no new discussion still ships a one line note rather than going silent"]}],"guidance":"Turn raw community activity into themed clusters with sentiment a team can actually use, never manufacturing volume to look consistent. recipes.name: Source Health Tracker
recipes.description: Track per-subreddit fetch health in `state/source_health.json`. After 3 consecutive failures, emit `reddit.source.unhealthy` and include a header line in the next digest recommending removal. Runs inline with uc_digest on every fetch.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_source_health","slug":"content-source-health-tracking","title":"Content source health tracking","status":"draft","path":"sales_marketing/community-channels","domain":"sales_marketing","description":{"need":"A source that has quietly stopped yielding anything looks identical to a quiet one, so dead entries stay on a follow list forever and spend budget every pass.","input":"The outcome of each fetch against each followed source, and the record of when each last produced something usable.","coreAction":"Distinguish a source that is quiet from a source that is broken by requiring a clear run of failures before saying anything, then recommend removal rather than continuing to poll.","output":"Each followed source carries a current health state, and a source that has been failing long enough is named for removal in the next digest."},"activities":[{"id":"observe","label":"Record the outcome of each fetch against each source","kind":"observe"},{"id":"assess","label":"Decide whether the pattern is quiet or broken","kind":"decide"},{"id":"flag","label":"Raise a source whose failures have become a clear pattern","kind":"act"},{"id":"recommend","label":"Carry a removal recommendation into the next digest","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"dead-sources-surfaced","statement":"A source that has stopped yielding usable content long enough to be dead weight gets flagged for removal instead of silently wasting fetch budget forever.","successCriteria":["A source failing repeatedly enough to be a pattern raises a health signal and a removal recommendation in the next digest","A single failure or a genuinely quiet period does not raise anything"]}],"guidance":"Track whether each followed source is still worth fetching, as a background responsibility to the digest rather than a job of its own. recipes.description: Scheduled scan of configured RSS/Atom feeds. Deduplicates, age-filters, and runs each new item through the curation pipeline. Caps per run to keep API usage predictable. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default daily 8am.

recipes.name: Weekly Maintenance
recipes.description: Weekly audit: orphaned-page detection, taxonomy consolidation suggestions, curation stats. Doesn't mutate automatically — surfaces suggestions via Messages for human action. Cadence is managed at the trigger-composition step; default Friday 6pm.

recipes.name: Alert & Outreach
recipes.description: Event-driven: on threshold crossings posts contextual messaging alerts (channel + owner DM) and drafts personalized email outreach (retention for churn, consultative upgrade for expansion) with 14-day suppression. Persists predictions and outreach to memory for monthly reconciliation.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_alert_and_outreach","slug":"revenue-signal-alerting-and-outreach","title":"Revenue signal alerting and outreach","status":"draft","path":"customer_support/retention","domain":"customer_support","description":{"need":"Money that was going to arrive and did not, and accounts drifting toward leaving or ready to grow, all fail quietly. recipes.name: Monthly Revenue Report & Calibration
recipes.description: Compiles the month's MRR waterfall from Stripe, health distribution from local state, and prediction accuracy from the log. Adjusts scoring weights based on precision/recall. Delivers a comprehensive report to the messaging channel #revenue-reports and the finance team via email. Default 1st of month 09:00 — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Payment Event Scan & Scoring
recipes.description: Polls Stripe for payment events, enriches with CRM customer context, computes churn risk and expansion readiness scores, and detects threshold crossings. Emits downstream events for alerting and outreach. Default every 5 minutes — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Classify and Route
recipes.description: Receives webhook payloads, classifies source/event/priority via three-tier logic, loads the matching routing rule, transforms the payload for each destination, and fan-outs. Logs every event for traceability.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_classify_and_route","slug":"webhook-classification-and-routing","title":"Webhook classification and routing","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/event-routing","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"Incoming events arrive in every shape from every system, and without one door that classifies and fans them out they either reach nobody or reach everybody.","input":"An incoming payload, the routing rules currently in force, and the record of payloads already processed.","coreAction":"Classify the payload accurately enough that the right rule applies, transform it for each destination it names, and treat losing an event as the one unacceptable outcome.","output":"The event delivered to every destination its rule names, or landed in a durable fallback, and never delivered twice."},"activities":[{"id":"receive","label":"Take the incoming payload whatever shape it arrives in","kind":"observe"},{"id":"classify","label":"Classify it by source, kind and priority","kind":"decide"},{"id":"match","label":"Find the rule that applies, or fall through to the unclassified path","kind":"decide"},{"id":"transform","label":"Shape the payload for each destination it names","kind":"act"},{"id":"deliver","label":"Fan out to every destination, with a durable fallback if all fail","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"no-event-lost","statement":"Every incoming event reaches its correct destination, and none are ever silently lost.","successCriteria":["An event is classified by source, type, and priority, then delivered to every destination its routing rule names","An event that fails every destination still lands in a durable fallback rather than disappearing","Urgent priority events are gated through human approval when the team has chosen that"]}],"guidance":"Own making sure every incoming event actually gets where it needs to go. Classify accurately enough that the routing rule applies correctly, and fan out to every named destination, transforming the payload as each one needs. Treat losing an event as the one unacceptable outcome; when everything else fails, it still lands in a durable fallback. Respect whether the team wants urgent events gated through approval.","connectorTypes":["messaging","knowledge_base","spreadsheet","email"],"recommendedTrigger":{"kind":"event","rationale":"An external system posting a payload is as literal an external event as this corpus contains, and the work has no existence apart from it. recipes.name: Manage Rules
recipes.description: Parses natural-language rule updates from the user ('Route Shopify to #ecommerce'), rewrites `routing_rules.json`, and confirms the diff. The rules take effect on the next webhook.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_manage_rules","slug":"routing-rule-management","title":"Event routing rule management","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/event-routing","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"Routing rules are edited in a file by hand or not at all, so they drift from what anyone actually wants and conflicts between them are discovered by an event going to the wrong place.","input":"A plain language instruction from a person, the rules currently in force, and the history of how this person phrases rules.","coreAction":"Translate the instruction into a correct rule, catch when it conflicts with one already configured, and ask one clarifying question rather than guessing.","output":"Rules that reflect what was actually asked for, confirmed back with a diff, and a surfaced conflict rather than a silent overwrite."},"activities":[{"id":"read","label":"Take the plain language instruction","kind":"observe"},{"id":"translate","label":"Translate it into a rule against the rules in force","kind":"decide"},{"id":"conflict","label":"Check it against existing rules and surface any conflict","kind":"decide"},{"id":"confirm","label":"Show the diff and apply only what was confirmed","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"rules-reflect-intent","statement":"The routing rules always reflect what the user actually asked for, with no silent conflicts.","successCriteria":["A plain language rule change is correctly translated into the rules and confirmed back to the user with a diff","A new rule that conflicts with an existing one is surfaced for the user to resolve, never silently overwritten or silently ignored"]}],"guidance":"Own translating the user's plain language routing intent into correct, working rules, and catching when a new instruction conflicts with what is already configured. recipes.name: Sentry Issue Scan
recipes.description: Queries Sentry for unresolved issues in scoped projects over the lookback window, filters by severity threshold, applies memory to auto-deprioritize known-noise patterns, and emits qualified issues to the root-cause capability. Default daily 8 AM — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_issue_scan","slug":"production-error-issue-filter","title":"Production error issue filter","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/error-triage","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"Root cause analysis is expensive per issue, so anything that reaches it must be worth investigating; a filter that passes everything makes the analysis step useless.","input":"Unresolved issues from the error monitor for the scoped projects and window, their occurrence counts, and the record of which patterns have been dismissed as noise.","coreAction":"Apply the occurrence floor and the learned noise patterns to decide which issues are worth an investigation, without forming an opinion about what caused them.","output":"A qualified set handed to root cause analysis, or a brief all clear when nothing qualifies."},"activities":[{"id":"query","label":"Query unresolved issues for the scoped projects and window","kind":"observe"},{"id":"floor","label":"Drop issues below the occurrence floor","kind":"decide"},{"id":"suppress","label":"Suppress patterns dismissed as noise often enough to have earned it","kind":"decide"},{"id":"hand-on","label":"Hand the qualified set on, or report a brief all clear","kind":"deliver"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"only-real-signal-reaches-root-cause","statement":"The root cause step only ever sees issues worth investigating, because known noise patterns are filtered before they get there.","successCriteria":["An issue below the severity threshold or matching a known-noise pattern is not forwarded.","Three or more noise dismissals of a pattern measurably suppress it going forward."]}],"guidance":"Pull unresolved issues for the window and hand only the ones worth investigating to root cause analysis: apply the occurrence floor and let memory of past noise dismissals suppress patterns that keep turning out to be nothing. Another monitoring connector will resolve this type but is unlikely to carry the same unresolved issue and occurrence count concepts."}],"lessons":[],"provenance":{"fromRecipes":["7a90ad49-bf04-5235-9f46-9b42bc6ee230"],"fromTemplates":["sentry-production-monitor"],"sourceTemplateId":"sentry-production-monitor"},"inputSchema":[{"name":"severity_threshold","type":"number","default":5,"min":1,"max":1000,"description":"Minimum occurrence count to surface an issue. Below = skipped."},{"name":"lookback_hours","type":"number","default":24,"min":1,"max":168,"description":"Scan window in hours. Match to your run cadence."},{"name":"environment_filter","type":"text","default":"production","description":"Environment tag to filter by, such as production, staging, or a comma-separated list."}]}

recipes.name: Codebase Root Cause Analysis
recipes.description: For each qualified issue, fetches the latest event for the full stack trace, reads source code at the error location across scoped codebases, traces cross-project callers, classifies root cause, and composes a Jira-format report with 3 ranked resolutions. One message per issue; each routes through human triage. Fires on `sentry.issue.qualified` events.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_root_cause","slug":"source-grounded-error-root-cause-analysis","title":"Source-grounded error root cause analysis","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/error-triage","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"A root cause report written from the stack trace alone restates what the recipes.name: Skill-Update Issue Writer
recipes.description: Event-driven capability. Subscribes to `review_decision.approved` (filtered to this persona's own reviews). Fetches the review's context_data via IPC callback, builds a unified diff, and POSTs an issue to GitHub or GitLab (selected by issue_platform) with labels and a `Skill-Ref: <slug>` footer. Emits `skill.update.issue_created` on success.

recipes.name: Skill Audit & Proposal
recipes.description: Scheduled + manual capability. Default cadence Monday 09:00 local — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Daily Escalation Digest
recipes.description: Queries knowledge base for today's escalations plus 7-day history, compiles stats (counts, tier breakdown, top offenders, avg breach duration, WoW trend), and emails a styled HTML digest to the support lead. Default weekdays 6 PM — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: SLA Breach Watch & Escalation
recipes.description: Polls support platform for tickets approaching or past SLA, classifies severity by tier, enriches with repeat-offender + agent-overload patterns, posts formatted messaging layout escalations to the messaging channel (DM to lead on Critical), and logs every escalation in knowledge base. recipes.description: Queries the database for new responses, validates and normalizes, runs sentiment + theme + NPS analysis, compares against rolling baselines, and flags anomalies. Default daily 09:00 — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Review Cycle
recipes.description: Periodic review of accepted ADRs: checks whether constraints still hold, presents a review batch with Reaffirm / Re-evaluate / Deprecate options, archives stale deprecated decisions. Default weekly Monday 09:00 — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.
recipes.prompt_template: {"id":"uc_review_cycle","slug":"decision-record-rot-watch","title":"Decision record rot watch","status":"draft","path":"software_engineering/engineering-records","domain":"software_engineering","description":{"need":"A decision stays presented as current long after the thing it assumed stopped being true, and the reader who arrives at the old record has no way to tell.","input":"The recorded decisions with the assumption each rests on, when each was last examined, and signals that something assumed has moved.","coreAction":"Watch the assumptions rather than the dates, and never silently reaffirm: if nothing has changed, say that nothing has changed.","output":"Decisions whose assumptions were contradicted reopened rather than left standing, and a superseded decision that points at what replaced it."},"activities":[{"id":"watch","label":"Watch for a dependency replaced, a constraint lifted, a service retired","kind":"observe"},{"id":"select","label":"Concentrate on the records most likely to be wrong rather than a rota","kind":"decide"},{"id":"present","label":"Put each due decision to a person to reaffirm, re-evaluate or deprecate","kind":"deliver"},{"id":"point","label":"Make a replacement findable from the old record, not only from the new one","kind":"act"},{"id":"archive","label":"Archive a deprecated decision once nothing active still references it","kind":"act"}],"outcomes":[{"id":"nothing-current-that-is-no-longer-true","statement":"No decision is still presented as current after the reasoning that supported it stopped being true.","successCriteria":["Each record carries the assumption it depended on","A decision whose assumption is contradicted is reopened rather than left standing","A superseded decision points at what replaced it, because the reader arrives at the old record first"]},{"id":"no-silent-reaffirmation-and-no-premature-archive","statement":"A due decision is judged by a person, and an archive never The v2 Monday cron and its thirty day review period turned staleness into an age, which is exactly the substitution the superseding responsibility rejects."},"personalizationNeeds":["Which assumptions the operator considers load bearing versus incidental, because every decision rests on dozens and only a few decide whether it is still right","How much code activity around a decision counts as a signal here, since that is the cheapest available proxy for an assumption moving"],"dependencies":[],"examples":[{"title":"A note store as the knowledge_base connector","connector":"obsidian","connectorType":"knowledge_base","notes":"Reopening and cross referencing decisions writes back into the same store the capture and linking recipes use."},{"title":"A repository as the source_control connector","connector":"github","connectorType":"source_control","notes":"Code activity in the area a decision governs is the signal this recipe leans on. recipes.name: Paid-Organic Cannibalization Watch

recipes.name: Error Classification
recipes.description: AI-classifies each ingested error across four dimensions: category (one of 7), root cause (pattern + dependency + temporal correlation), impact (blast radius + severity), and remediation (specific actionable fix). Stores classification back into the error index. Fires on `workflow.error.ingested` events.

recipes.name: Error Event Ingestion
recipes.description: Subscribes to platform error events from every persona and polls the execution API every 10 minutes to catch silent failures. Normalizes each error into a structured record, deduplicates within a 1-hour window, and appends to the 90-day rolling error index. Default poll every 10 minutes — final cadence set at the trigger-composition step.

recipes.name: Cross-Workflow Pattern Detection
recipes.description: Runs four pattern checks on each classified error: recurring (same pattern 3+ in 1h), cascading (dependent persona fails within 15m), time-based clustering, service-wide outage (3+ personas on same service in 30m). Sends real-time critical alerts and emits pattern events for downstream automation. Fires on `workflow.error.classified` events.

Incremental — each run advances coverage on a new area until the target is met.

recipes.name: Accepted idea delivery to the main branch
recipes.description: An accepted idea that nobody carries to the main branch is a decision that never happened, and the work already exists in pieces that each own a different hand-off: one triages, one implements, one gives a test verdict, one releases. Nothing owns the item's identity from accepted to merged, nothing re-checks the idea against the code as it stands before building it, and nothing looks afterwards to see whether the change did what the idea claimed. Carry each accepted item this run was named all the way to a reviewable, verified change on the main branch: re-validate it against the current code with the authority to decline and say why, derive the checklist that will prove it done, implement it in an isolated branch, let the repository's own checks and tests be the standard, deliver a pull request or a ready branch where no hosted review surface exists, and after the merge check the claim the idea made.

recipes.name: Project KPI and coverage stewardship
recipes.description: A project's context map, use cases and KPIs decay quietly: contexts nobody has scanned since the code moved, groups carrying no KPI at all, KPIs with a target and no measurement behind it, and a backlog that is either empty or full of items nobody has looked at in months. None of it announces itself, because each number lives on a different screen and no single reading puts them beside each other. Keep the project's measurement loop honest and moving: read the coverage, decide which gap this cycle is worth closing, populate the backlog with concrete items that carry their evidence, get them executed through the delivery loop, and back-measure so every claim that something improved is a number that moved rather than a description of work done.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Enterprise solution design across a workspace
recipes.name: Enterprise solution design across a workspace
recipes.description: An owner states a goal in the language of the business and the work starts anyway, one repository at a time, with nobody holding the whole. Two teams then own the same data under different names, a responsibility nobody claimed turns out to belong to everyone, the integration style is decided by whichever service was written first, and the load the system was supposed to carry is discovered at the end. None of that is visible from inside a single project, because a boundary is only wrong when seen against the boundary beside it. Decide where the seams of the system fall: which bounded contexts exist, which services carry which responsibility, who owns each piece of data, how the parts talk to each other and how much of that is asynchronous, what the non functional envelope is, and what is deliberately out of scope. Name each context against an external ontology the domain already has, so a boundary can be argued against something other than taste, and designate which parts of the system carry value that cannot be recreated, because those parts earn obligations the rest do not. Hold the design against reality as the projects build, and revise it when their evidence contradicts a boundary rather than defending the drawing.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Goal direction and channel authority across projects
recipes.name: Goal direction and channel authority across projects
recipes.description: A design becomes real only through goals somebody set and direction somebody gave, and both fail in the same quiet way. Goals get written once at the start and then drift from the design nobody reread, so the projects work hard on the wrong thing. Direction is spoken in a register the listener cannot tell from a suggestion, so an instruction is treated as a thought and a thought is treated as an order. And when two projects want opposite things, each argues locally with the owner who cannot decide it, because the only reader who can see both is the one who never came back to look. Keep every project's goals traceable to the design and current against it, and speak into the shared channel with the register said out loud: a directive is an instruction that expects the work done, a request expects an answer, a note is context that expects nothing. Phrase a directive as an acceptance criterion drawn from a standard the domain already holds rather than as an outcome you want, because a criterion somebody else wrote can be met or missed and an outcome you phrased yourself can only be argued about. Then read what came back, chase the directives nobody answered, and decide the conflicts between projects that no single project can settle.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Project portfolio composition from a solution design
recipes.name: Project portfolio composition from a solution design
recipes.description: A solution design that never becomes projects is a drawing. The step from one to the other is where portfolios go wrong quietly: a service in the design that nobody created a home for, a repository that exists on disk but was never registered so no persona can reach it, a project standing with no owner because adoption was left for later, two projects that both believe they own the same context, and a project created with no goal at all, whose team then invents its own direction from whatever it can see. Turn the design into a portfolio that matches it: create each missing repository and register it as a project in the workspace in one act, have each project declare itself in a machine readable file the moment it exists, adopt an App Master on each with the charters that context actually needs, set each project's first goals from the design's own words, then read the portfolio back against the design and resolve every orphan, every duplicate owner and every project standing without direction.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Scope reflection on personas' own proposals and lessons
recipes.name: Scope reflection on personas' own proposals and lessons
recipes.description: The people doing the work are the first to see where their scope is wrong, and in an organisation of agents they say so in writing: a proposal to take on a responsibility nobody holds, to give one up, to split one that turned out to be two. Those proposals then sit unread, because reading them is nobody's job and answering one means deciding whether it changes a single charter or the whole design. The same happens to lessons: each one is filed where it was learned, so the next holder of the same work learns it again from scratch. Read what the workers proposed about their own scope and decide, for each one, what it would actually change: a charter, the design, a gate, or nothing. A gate is the verdict whenever the lesson is mechanical and would otherwise be a paragraph nobody reads at the moment it matters, because a rule that generalises should refuse the mistake rather than describe it. Apply the ones that hold, decline the rest with a reason the proposer can argue with, and separate the lessons that only apply where they were learned from the ones any holder of that work would want, promoting only the second kind.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Workforce planning across a project portfolio
recipes.name: Workforce planning across a project portfolio
recipes.description: Work stalls for a reason nobody writes down: a responsibility that has no holder. Each project owner feels it locally and asks for help in their own words, so the same missing role gets requested three times under three names while a role that was hired for work that has since ended keeps its seat. Nothing reads the asks together, nothing compares them against what the goals are actually doing, and a request written as a job title carries none of the evidence a hiring system would need to compose anything useful from it. Decide which roles the workspace is actually missing, by reading the owners' asks against the evidence in the goals rather than taking each ask at face value, and describe each real gap as the work it is: what has to be done, what evidence says it is not being done now, how anyone would know the role succeeded, and what the role is allowed and not allowed to touch. Send that to the hiring system, judge what comes back against the need as written, and retire the roles whose work has ended.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Abuse path smoke suite where the rejection is the subject
recipes.name: Abuse path smoke suite where the rejection is the subject
recipes.description: A test suite proves the happy path and then stops, so the only requests anybody exercises are the ones a well behaved client sends. The rejection path is the one an attacker walks and the one nobody tests, and it fails in two directions at once: a route that answers a request carrying no credential has already leaked, and a route that answers a malformed one with a server error has told the caller that the guard was never reached. Worse than either, a suite of invalid requests that has only ever been green has never been shown to detect anything, so its greenness is evidence of nothing at all. Build a suite in which every request is invalid by construction, and assert the exact status class each abuse must produce rather than asserting that nothing broke. A 200 on any probe is a finding and a 5xx on any probe is a finding, because the first means the guard did not run and the second means something behind it answered instead. Then prove the suite itself by weakening one route on purpose and watching it turn red.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Architecture decision records with decision status split from delivery status
recipes.name: Architecture decision records with decision status split from delivery status
recipes.description: A decision record says accepted and everyone downstream reads it as built. They are two different facts with two different owners and two different dates, and collapsing them costs twice: a compliance answer cites an accepted decision whose implementation was never deployed, and a team builds against a control that exists only in a document. This is not hypothetical. In the reference this work is designed against, one decision stands accepted while the compliance mapping that reads it records its topology as not deployed, and an independent review control reads restored, narrowed to a fraction of the fleet, and advisory rather than required, while the decision behind it says only that it was accepted. Record the decision and its delivery as two statuses that move independently and carry their own dates. Accepted says a choice was made and by whom; delivered says how much of it exists in the code and what proves it. Revisit the second whenever the code moves, name the scope wherever delivery covered less than the decision decided, and never let the first status imply the second.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Contract first API stewardship across three version axes
recipes.name: Contract first API stewardship across three version axes
recipes.description: A service has three versions and most teams keep one. The contract it publishes, the routes it actually serves and the artefact it releases each move for their own reason, and collapsing them into a single number makes every one of them wrong: a breaking change ships under a patch bump because the release axis never noticed, a route is served that no consumer could have planned for because it was never published, and a published route answers 404 because it was removed and the document was not. In an organisation where several agents change the same portfolio in the same hour, a single shared version file makes it worse still, because it is a merge conflict by construction and every worker meets it. Keep the published contract, the served routes and the released artefact on three separate axes and in agreement: publish before you serve, move the contract's major only when the contract breaks and carry that break into the route prefix, and move the release on its own trigger. Reconcile in both directions, because a route served but unpublished and a route published but unserved are different defects and only one of them looks like a missing feature.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Gate authorship from a recurring defect
recipes.name: Gate authorship from a recurring defect
recipes.description: A defect that has happened twice will happen a third time, and the usual answer is a paragraph. The paragraph is read by the people who already knew, and the next author, who never read it, ships the same defect again. The mechanical answer fails differently and worse: a check written in a hurry passes forever, is never once seen to fail, and is trusted precisely because it has never objected to anything. The reference this is written against names that failure in its own manifest header, that a gate which has only ever passed is unfalsified, and answers it by running the proof of reachable failure before the check and skipping the check when that proof gives the wrong verdict. Decide what the occurrences have in common, and whether that common thing is checkable by a machine rather than by a reader's attention. Where it is, declare it as one entry in the project's manifest carrying four things a check cannot be trusted without: how many subjects it expects to find, the reason it exists in the words of the defect it prevents, a date it should be argued with again, and a proof that its failing state is reachable. Where it is not mechanically checkable, say so and leave it as prose rather than shipping a check that cannot fail.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Governance drift audit of declarations against code
recipes.name: Governance drift audit of declarations against code
recipes.description: Every declaration in a governed system is a claim about the code. A decision record claims a control exists, a charter claims an agent may reach exactly these tools and no others, a manifest claims a set of checks runs, a baseline claims a number that has been held. Each was true the day it was written and nothing rereads it, so the governance surface slowly becomes an accurate description of a codebase that no longer exists. The worst case is not a claim that fails loudly. It is a check that quietly stopped running while every report continued to say success, which is a failure that looks exactly like health. Read every declaration against the code that would prove it, and keep three verdicts apart: a claim the code confirms, a claim the code refutes, and a claim nothing could have tested either way. Include the checks themselves in the audit rather than trusting their verdicts, because a verifier that can be switched off by the thing it verifies is not one. Then propose every correction and make none of them.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Load envelope authorship and measured ceiling reporting
recipes.name: Load envelope authorship and measured ceiling reporting
recipes.description: Load targets are usually adjectives dressed as engineering. A system is said to handle a million users, and the number came from the ambition rather than from anything anybody ran, so it can never be met or missed. When a run does happen the second failure arrives: the percentiles are read from a run where a share of the requests never answered, which quietly removes the slowest work from the sample and reports a system faster than the one that exists. The reference this is written against puts the rule in every one of its read baselines, that a route which did not answer 200 invalidates the percentile, and asserts a failed request rate under 0.01 with a checks rate of exactly 1.0 beside it. State the target as five numbers before anything runs: how much data is seeded, what rate is sustained, for how long, at which latency percentile, and what error rate invalidates the result. Then run it, apply the error rule before reading a single percentile, and report the machine's own resource ceiling beside the latency figures, because a percentile with no ceiling next to it cannot be compared to any other run. Where a larger figure is wanted, derive it as arithmetic from what was measured and label it as arithmetic.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Money path service certification against a declared contract
recipes.name: Money path service certification against a declared contract
recipes.description: A service carrying nine of its ten obligations reads exactly like one carrying ten, and the difference only shows on the day the missing one was the one that mattered. The obligations that protect money are the ones nobody notices missing: a write endpoint that shipped without an idempotency key, a domain layer that quietly took a framework dependency, a migration with no rollback note, a timestamp read from the wall clock instead of an injected one. The reference this work is written against states the cost in the rationale of its own gate `idempotency-coverage-money-path`: a duplicate POST on a money path endpoint is a double debit, and without a ratchet a new endpoint ships without a key and nothing objects. Read one service against the contract its own project declared, obligation by obligation, and give each one a verdict backed by the file that carries it or the absence that proves it missing. Keep three verdicts apart rather than two: carried, absent, and not checkable from here, because a certification that cannot tell absent from unlooked at is worth nothing. File every gap as an idea naming the obligation it violates, and change no code, because a reader that repairs what it finds stops being able to report what it found.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Regulatory acceptance mapping to controls and evidence
recipes.name: Regulatory acceptance mapping to controls and evidence
recipes.description: A compliance claim costs nothing to write and everything to defend. The usual document lists regulations beside the words compliant or in progress, which tells a reader neither what satisfies the requirement nor where to look for proof, and the first person to ask for the proof discovers that half the rows were intentions. The reference this is written against solved it with a shape rather than a longer document: one table, one artefact path per requirement, and a named gap written in wherever no artefact exists. Its own evidence pack does exactly that for DORA, mapping Art. 5 and 6 to `docs/bcp/dora-ictrm.md` and `docs/threat-models/`, Art. 8 to per service SBOMs and a third party register, Art. 9 to policy authorization and pull request time vulnerability checks, and Art. 11(3)(c) to `docs/bcp/dr-test-log.md`, and it names four gaps rather than rounding them up. Break one named regulation into requirements small enough that a single control can answer each, decide which control does answer it, then go and look for the artefact that would evidence that control to somebody who does not trust you. A requirement whose artefact exists becomes a row. A requirement whose artefact does not exist yet becomes a named gap with what would close it, never a row with an intention in the evidence column, because a matrix is only worth reading if its rows are the ones that could survive being checked.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Service self declaration and lineage maintenance
recipes.name: Service self declaration and lineage maintenance
recipes.description: What a service holds, where it holds it, how long it must keep it and who it reads from are questions asked at the worst possible moments: during an incident, during an audit, and when a schema changes under a consumer nobody knew existed. Answered from a hand written architecture document they are answered wrongly, because a document describing seventy odd services has already drifted from the directory listing by the time anyone rereads it. And a declaration nobody checks is worse than no declaration at all: it carries the authority of a fact while being a claim, and the lineage edge it names may have been deleted a year ago. Keep one small declaration per service holding only the facts a person decides and a build cannot derive: the data domain it belongs to, its primary store and the database it owns, the classification of what it holds, its retention period, and its lineage in both directions with the relation type and what flows across each edge. Then hold every declared edge against the code, because a declaration whose edges nobody verifies is a claim wearing a fact's clothes.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Threat model for a money path service
recipes.name: Threat model for a money path service
recipes.description: Most threat models are written once, at the moment somebody asked for one, and are wrong within a quarter. The model itself is rarely the problem: the problem is that the service kept moving and the model did not. A new caller, a new queue, a credential that started being read by something else, a boundary that used to be inside one process and is now a network hop, and the document still describes a system that no longer exists while carrying the authority of one that was reviewed. The reference this is written against treats a structured model as a definition of done artefact under ADR-0030 D2, at `docs/threat-models/<service>.md`, and its checker fails the pipeline if any money path service lacks a structured one; gate `threat-model-coverage` enforces that, and 45 models exist under it. Trace where this service's data crosses a boundary somebody else controls, work each crossing through the threat categories, and decide for each credible threat whether it is mitigated, deliberately accepted or still open, saying who accepted what. Write it in the structured form the project can check rather than as prose. Then do the part the first authoring never covers: read every change to the service for a moved trust boundary, and reopen the model in the same change that moved it, because a model updated later is a model that was wrong in between.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Acceptance certification by representative users across two levels
recipes.name: Acceptance certification by representative users across two levels
recipes.description: A project's own checks answer whether the code does what its authors meant. Nothing in them answers whether a representative user can finish the job they came for, at a standard a senior person in that role would accept. So a project accumulates green gates and shipping waves while a journey nobody walks end to end has been broken for a month. The two honest failures are opposite and both common: certifying only against a model of the surface, which is cheap and never touches the running system, and certifying only in a live browser, which is slow enough that it happens once and then never again. Certify the project's journeys through the eyes of its representative users at two levels with different costs and different truth. Run the cheap theoretical level over the surface the code describes after every merged wave, because it is affordable often enough to catch a regression the week it lands. Run the empirical level against the running system once per act, because it is the only level that can contradict the first one. Judge each journey through its user's own lens rather than against a feature list, and file every finding as an item the project delivers.

recipes.source_use_case_name: Gate authorship as a project owner's answer to a recurring defect
recipes.name: Gate authorship as a project owner's answer to a recurring defect
recipes.description: A defect happens, gets fixed, and the fix ends as a sentence: a line in a conventions file, a paragraph in a review, a lesson on a charter. Then it happens again, to a different author who never read the sentence, and the second fix produces a second sentence. Prose is read by the people who already agree with it, which is why the only reader a written rule reliably reaches is its author. Meanwhile the manifest of mechanical checks belongs to another project, so writing into it means asking somebody else, and asking is exactly the step that a note lets you skip. Decide which of this project's recurring defects is a rule rather than an accident, and answer it with a check in the shared manifest rather than another sentence. That means proving recurrence before proposing, deciding whether the rule generalises past this project or belongs only here, carrying the proposal to whoever owns the manifest instead of writing into their project unasked, and then keeping the check alive afterwards: honouring its review date, graduating it from advisory to enforced or retiring it, and noticing when it has quietly stopped finding anything.
